subject.title: feat(loop): implement autonomous agent loop (/loop) with token budget guard

question: Should OpenClaw add a new user-facing core loop controller, or should autonomous multi-step work remain composed from `/goal`, Task Flow, tasks, and subagents?
rationale: The proposal creates a permanent command, tool, lifecycle, persistence, and safety surface that overlaps existing orchestration architecture, so implementation details cannot settle whether this product abstraction should exist in core.

options.title: Use existing orchestration
options.body: Keep core on `/goal`, Task Flow, tasks, and subagents, and narrow the paired issue to any concrete missing primitive discovered while composing them.

options.title: Sponsor a core loop
options.body: Approve a new core abstraction, then require a fresh architecture proposal defining ownership, persistence, accounting, interruption, permissions, and cross-surface behavior before implementation.

options.title: Prototype externally
options.body: Develop the workflow as a plugin, skill, or external controller first and use real-world evidence to identify any missing generic core API.

recommendation.title: Use existing orchestration
recommendation.body: Keep core on `/goal`, Task Flow, tasks, and subagents, and narrow the paired issue to any concrete missing primitive discovered while composing them.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice spans core agent runtime, CLI, Gateway, security, and orchestration boundaries listed under this owner's repository responsibilities.
